summary: I sent the scripted prompt. The agent loaded hyperpowers:requesting-code-review, read the code-reviewer.md template and dispatched a general-purpose reviewer subagent with the Agent tool. The review came back "Not ready to merge". It has two Critical findings: the pagination off-by-one at src/handlers.js:18 and the unawaited saveOrder at src/handlers.js:37. None of the six code areas the story lists as correct got a blocking finding. The agent asked no follow-up questions, so no scripted answers were needed.
reasoning: Every acceptance criterion is met. The skill loaded, the reviewer went out through the Agent tool with the template, and both seeded defects came back as Critical with file:line, a concrete input and its outcome. The review does not approve the change. None of the code areas the story lists as correct got a Critical or Important finding. The only criticisms of withRetry, config.json and the fixture are under Minor, which the story allows.

observations.description: In the parent's summary to the user, file:line references were dropped for Important #4 (no line) and #6 ("this file", no line). The subagent's full review had them (test/handlers.test.js:29-32 and src/handlers.js:15-16). The user sees a less precise version than the reviewer wrote.

Side effect outside the workdir: the agent ran `cd /Users/johnss51/Development/agents/hyperpowers && bash skills/requesting-code-review/scripts/codex-preflight` and then `... scripts/ungated-ledger append --class degraded-gate ...`. That writes ledger state into the main hyperpowers repo, not the project under review. The skill also resolved its files from the .worktrees/adoption-remediation-treatment plugin dir, yet the scripts ran from the repo root, which may be a different checkout.
While the reviewer subagent ran in the background, the parent polled with `sleep 60` and then `sleep 120` Bash calls instead of waiting for a completion notification. The whole run took about 4m45s.
The agent printed an unprompted Codex install nag ("/plugin marketplace add openai/codex-plugin-cc ...") in the middle of the review, which adds noise for the user.

Some Important findings could reasonably be Minor, especially #5 (fractional/negative page validation) and #7 (client-supplied createdAt). The ranking stays sensible because the parent says only 1–4 block the merge.
On first launch, both the workspace-trust and bypass-permissions dialogs default to "No, exit", so each needs Down+Enter. This is expected Claude Code behavior, noted only for harness authors.

criteria.criterion: Invoked requesting-code-review skill and dispatched reviewer subagent via Agent tool
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use sequence: `Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:requesting-code-review"}`, then Read of skills/requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md, then `Agent {"subagent_type":"general-purpose","description":"Review code changes","prompt":"You are a Senior Code Reviewer...`. A subagent log was created at subagents/agent-ad77b24baa28f240d.jsonl.

criteria.criterion: Pagination offset in listOrdersHandler flagged Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Final report, under Critical: "1. Off-by-one makes page 1 unreachable — src/handlers.js:18 ... const offset = page * size; // treats it as 0-based ... {page: 1, size: 10} returns ord_00000010..019 instead of 000..009"

criteria.criterion: Unawaited store.saveOrder in createOrderHandler flagged Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Final report, under Critical: "2. saveOrder never awaited — src/handlers.js:37 ... the client gets 201 Created for an order that was never stored, and the unhandled rejection takes the Node process down"
Parent: "## Reviewer verdict: **Not ready to merge**". Subagent: "**Ready to merge?** No"

criteria.criterion: No blocking finding against the listed correct-as-written items (header)
criteria.evidence: Criteria 6–11 below each pass. The listed items appear only under Minor or Strengths, never under Critical or Important.

Only Minor mentions: "8. retryAttempts: 0 throws undefined. src/util.js:8-18" and "9. Retry wraps an operation that cannot fail transiently". The Strengths section says "withRetry backoff is correctly implemented with the original error preserved".

criteria.criterion: config.js readFileSync not flagged as blocking
criteria.evidence: Mentioned only under Minor: "10. Moving config into config.json is unrelated to both stated requirements. src/config.js:3-9".
No finding targets parseOrderId. The Strengths section says "ORDER_ID is properly anchored".

criteria.criterion: store.listOrders slice not flagged as blocking
criteria.evidence: No finding calls store.js listOrders wrong. It comes up only in Minor #9 ("store.listOrders is an in-memory slice; it has no transient failure mode"). Minor #11 cites store.js:16, but that is about duplicate ids.

criteria.criterion: Log-and-rethrow catch in listOrdersHandler not flagged as blocking
criteria.evidence: None of the Critical/Important findings 1–7 targets the catch. Minor #8 mentions that line 27 rethrows a non-Error only in the retryAttempts:0 case.

criteria.criterion: Fixed clock and seeded 25-order fixture not flagged as blocking
criteria.evidence: Important #3 criticizes the assertion ("asserts only the *count*"), not the fixture, and says "The fixture was deliberately seeded with identifiable ids". The fixture is praised in Strengths. Seeding is mentioned only in Minor #12 (test-order coupling).

criteria.criterion: Every Critical/Important finding cites file:line and states a trigger and outcome
criteria.evidence: Subagent review: #1 handlers.js:18, {page:1,size:10} gives 010..019. #2 handlers.js:37, non-positive total gives 201 and an unhandled rejection. #3 test/handlers.test.js:21-27, slice(10,20) passes green. #4 test/handlers.test.js:29-32, an await-and-assert-persisted test fails against current code. #5 handlers.js:16-18, {page:-1} gives 200 with an empty list. #6 handlers.js:15-16, listOrdersHandler() throws TypeError. #7 handlers.js:32,36, createdAt:"whenever" is accepted with 201. Caveat: the parent's condensed summary dropped the line numbers for #4 and #6.
